status: Project prospective checkpoint after v1.5, source/schema inspection and six owned CPU smoke forwards, but before new dataset inference. Not external preregistration.
split_contract: Outcome-independent salted-hash unique groups. BoolQ passage/OCNLI premise grouping, training-derived fit/dev and labeled official validation/dev for evaluation (no blind-test claim); TMMLUplus dataset-card dev/val/test files with round-robin subjects. Exact test groups excluded from calibration. One canonical request artifact shared by all models; gold in a separate analysis artifact.
clinc: Retrieval-assisted full 151-label prediction. TF-IDF char_wb 3:5, min_df 2, maximum similarity per intent, top eight of 150 intents plus OOS. Retriever uses original in-scope training excluding selected question groups. No gold inserted: shortlist misses count as errors. Pilot OOS fraction fixed at 25 percent, not the natural dataset fraction. Intent IDs/positions vary by query; the direction-aware controller's CLINC state represents candidate position, not a globally stable intent identity.
native_heads: Use original architecture, saved trained heads and native prompt rendering. Root NanoJev navigation checkpoint, not its later game-specific variants. Decider's checkpoint-native temperature and System One publisher T=1.75; no temperature fitting to test. Task records are semantically identical; tokenization/native prompt forms necessarily differ.
cpu_runtime: GitHub-hosted Ubuntu 24.04, four Torch threads, resident model inference, batch one request with candidate paths internally batched. NanoJev FP32; Qwen3.5 BF16 storage/output with disclosed FP32 Linear/Conv accumulation. No quantization, decoding, generated fallback or random-head fallback. Max 2048 native-path tokens, no truncation. Twelve shards; all three models sequentially on each same host, cyclically rotated order. Cache removed only from that job's dedicated model-cache directory.
optimization: Preserve candidate direction and fixed confidence bins instead of only answer-equality patterns. Fit a positive joint observation distribution with a directional-confusion factorized prior. Compile finite Bellman actions into version-bound arrays. Compare compiled decisions exactly with online expected-Q reconstruction; report compile/fit time and memory separately. This is finite-model optimization, not a novel universally optimal theorem.
selection: Fit likelihoods only on 32 fit cases per dataset; choose prior strength and gate only on 16 development cases. Model identities never change. Same-world myopic and independence ablations select their own strength where applicable. Development gate retains fit-selected single unless the candidate controller improves development objective by at least 0.01; this is a heuristic, not an out-of-sample safety guarantee.
metrics: Native full-coverage accuracy, Wilson intervals, per-dataset/host p50 p95 milliseconds, maximum/summed input tokens, proper multiclass Brier and clipped NLL, top-label ECE, selective coverage/accuracy/loss. CLINC retrieval recall and OOS recall/FPR separately. Cascade latency is reconstructed by summing actually measured same-host component times, not newly measured integrated online serving latency. Offline training/compile costs disclosed separately.
primary_contrasts: joint Bellman vs agreement-only at defer 0.25
joint Bellman vs fit-selected single at defer 0.25
development-gated vs fit-selected single at defer 0.25
joint Bellman vs agreement-only at defer 1.0
inference: 2000 paired group bootstraps within dataset with equal macro weights. 95 percent intervals and conservative 98.75 percent four-comparison intervals, conditional on one fitted/calibrated cohort. Not equivalence tests, no synthetic fake model rows.
limits: 128 test groups is a pilot, not full official benchmark scoring
Decider training includes BoolQ/CLINC families, not unseen-task evidence
NanoJev root navigation specialization is substantially out of domain
OCNLI and System One materials have noncommercial restrictions
Chinese is outside Decider's declared English language
No original-model training or inter-agent debate
CPU results are not GPU/service claims
An optimized fitted decision rule can still lose on test data
